content_of_post_to_answer: Do you find it easier to focus on a book when you are sitting in the same chair every day?
answer: The chair probably matters less because of comfort and more because the brain learns context. A familiar place becomes a cue that says “this is where reading happens,” reducing the small decisions and distractions that compete for attention. The interesting part is that this can work both ways: a place can train focus, but it can also train avoidance if we only ever read under perfect conditions. A strong reading habit is built when the environment supports focus, not when focus depends entirely on the environment.
